source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Avoid local comfort measures until the swelling resolves spontaneously.","B":"Use a warm sitz bath as the preferred first intervention immediately after birth.","C":"Apply an ice pack for short periods to reduce swelling and pain.","D":"Apply continuous dry heat to the perineum during the first 24 hours."}}
source_row.rationale: MedlinePlus postpartum instructions recommend ice packs during the first 24 hours after vaginal birth to reduce perineal swelling and pain. Warm baths are generally introduced after the first 24 hours.
source_row.source_detail: Perineal-care section: ice packs during the first 24 hours; warm baths after 24 hours. MedlinePlus patient instruction review date 2024-11-08; rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Basic Care and Comfort; hygiene, comfort, positioning and nonpharmacologic care activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

source_row.stem: A client is 8 hours postpartum after a vaginal birth and reports perineal swelling and soreness. Which comfort measure is appropriate during the first 24 hours?
